item.title: Tinubu defends borrowing plans, says investments ‘ll expand opportunities for future generations
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA —PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has responded to criticism, especially from opposition leaders, over new loans the country has accessed from international institutions and banks. ‎ ‎In an essay titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” to be published on Nigerian news platforms, President Tinubu wrote: “The real question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, what value we create and what future we leave behind.” ‎ ‎He identified the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid upgrades and the modernisation of key commercial ports in Lagos as major projects expected to strengthen Nigeria’s productive capacity. ‎ ‎The President said the projects, alongside investments in healthcare, education and vocational training, would connect economic regions, reduce logistics costs, unlock agricultural and industrial potential and attract private investment. ‎ ‎The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is expected to cut logistics costs along its corridor by 15 to 20 per cent. It could add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s GDP through expanded trade, tourism, and industrial activity. ‎ ‎The project is also projected to generate about 100,000 direct jobs in construction and engineering, alongside more than 150,000 indirect jobs in logistics, materials and related services. ‎ ‎According to him: “We are not simply building highways. We are opening economic corridors, connecting markets, unlocking industries and reshaping Nigeria’s economic geography.” ‎ ‎He said the administration’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2030 would require sustained infrastructure investment to support higher productivity, industrialisation and trade. ‎ ‎“We cannot build a USD 1 trillion economy with infrastructure designed for an economy a fraction of that size,” Tinubu said. ‎ ‎He wrote that improving economic indicators and growing international investor confidence are creating opportunities for Nigeria to attract long-term investment and expand critical infrastructure. ‎ ‎The President said the economic reforms his administration introduced in May 2023 helped restore macroeconomic stability, strengthen public finances, and improve the country’s standing in international financial markets. ‎ ‎He said a $1 trillion economy would not emerge by declaration alone but must be built through sustained investment, higher productivity, industrialisation, and trade, stressing that infrastructure development would be critical to achieving the target by 2030. ‎ ‎In an article titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier. ‎ ‎He also said gross external reserves rose to $55.1 billion as of October 9, 2026, including about $46 b

item.title: Osimhen welcomes second child with Cameroonian-German girlfriend
item.description: Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen and his girlfriend, Stefanie Ladewig, have welcomed their second child, a baby girl named Liora Audrey. Galatasaray, the Turkish club where Osimhen plays, announced the arrival of the couple’s daughter in a social media post on Thursday. “Our Football A Team player Victor Osimhen and Stefanie have welcomed a baby girl into the world. “We congratulate the couple Victor and Stefanie; we wish their newborn baby Liora Audrey a long, healthy, and happy life!” the post read. The couple’s first daughter, Hailey, was born in October 2022. Ladewig, a Cameroonian-German fashion model and social media influencer, reportedly began dating Osimhen in 2019 when the Nigerian forward was playing for German Bundesliga side Wolfsburg. Earlier this month, reports emerged that Ladewig had been involved in a road accident while heavily pregnant. Turkish media reported that she escaped unhurt in the crash, which involved three vehicles. Meanwhile, Osimhen is expected to feature for Galatasaray in their league fixture against T. Konyaspor on Friday, having been included in the squad for the match. The 27-year-old forward was in impressive form on Monday, scoring twice to help Galatasaray defeat their fierce Istanbul rivals, Fenerbahce, in the city derby. Galatasaray currently lead the league standings after nine matches, while Osimhen has scored eight goals, placing him among the competition’s joint-top scorers. item.title: Omitted candidates: INEC upholds 41 of governorship petitions, rejects 28
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has upheld 41 of the 69 petitions filed against the final list of governorship candidates for the 2027 general election, while rejecting 28. Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC) of the commission, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday night. According to him, the petitions came from 12 political parties across 26 states. He said, “The complaints concerned the omission of certain political parties, the wrongful inclusion of candidates of political parties whose names were not contained in the membership registers submitted by their political parties, and instances of alleged multiple nominations.” Haruna said the commission examined the complaints against its records and the law. “Following a review of the complaints, relevant records and applicable legal provisions, the Commission found merit in some representations and approved the inclusion of affected candidates and their political parties, while complaints found to be without merit were declined. “In addition, some names that were wrongfully published in the final list were removed after verifying that their names were not on the register. “The Commission also approved the removal of candidates whose nominations were found to be inconsistent with the applicable legal requirements,” the statement said. Although INEC did not name any candidate or state, a source had earlier revealed that the commission’s meeting on Thursday to review complaints from parties and candidates left out of the lists had cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections, subject to the outcome of pending court cases. The source also said the petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list, did not succeed. “Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said when asked about the PDP governorship candidate in Gombe State. “He did not succeed,” the source said when asked about Adebutu. On the State Houses of Assembly, the commission said the decisions affecting candidates sponsored by political parties “were informed by specific complaints received and determined in accordance with the law and the Commission’s established criteria.” For those elections, INEC received 61 petitions from 11 political parties across 11 states. Twenty-five succeeded, while 36 failed. The commission said the affected candidates, political parties and states “will be reflected in the updated list on the Commission’s website.” “Once again, the Commission assures the public of its commitment to transparency and the credibility of the electoral process,” the statement said. item.title: Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 to reach League Cup quarter-finals
item.description: Everton swept into the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win against Newcastle on Thursday as they booked a clash against giant-killers Fleetwood. David Moyes’s side took the lead through James Garner’s first-half goal at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. Hayden Hackney doubled the lead with his first goal since his close-season move from Middlesbrough. Everton striker Thierno Barry netted in the second half and Dan Burn’s reply for Newcastle came far too late to stop the Toffees ending their three-match winless run. Chasing their first League Cup final appearance in 43 years, Everton will travel to fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in the week commencing December 14. The ‘Cod Army’ caused one of the biggest shocks in League Cup history on Tuesday when they beat Premier League champions Arsenal in a penalty shoot-out after a 1-1 draw at Highbury. Everton have never won the League Cup, losing their two final appearances in 1977 and 1984. Everton fans do not need reminding that it is 31 years since the club won the FA Cup in their most recent trophy triumph. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a noted Everton fan, is old enough to remember that success and he was cheering from the stands as Moyes’s men made light work of their last-16 tie. Newcastle will have the chance for revenge when the sides meet again in the Premier League at St James’ Park on Monday. Everton dropped a pre-match bombshell, saying Jack Grealish was unavailable for selection “due to a breach of club discipline”. Grealish, beset by criticism of his behaviour off the pitch, was reported to have taken an unauthorised absence from training. But the on-loan Manchester City winger’s absence was no problem for his team-mates. – Everton hit their stride – Newcastle tested Jordan Pickford early on when Joe Willock’s low drive was palmed away by the Everton goalkeeper, who repelled Fabian Schar’s long-range strike moments later. Garner steadied Everton’s nerves with a clinical opener in the 34th minute. Hackney teed up Garner just inside the area and the midfielder stretched to guide a fine finish into the far corner for his first goal since January. Everton had hit their stride and Hackney struck on the stroke of half-time. At the climax of a blistering Everton counter-attack, Barry hooked a cross into the six-yard box and Hackney timed his run perfectly to volley past Lukas Hornicek. Frustrated Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Joelinton, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa at the interval. Wissa had an immediate chance after sprinting onto Willock’s pass, but he misjudged the high bounce and ended up heading straight at Pickford. It was a costly miss as Barry put the result beyond doubt in the 69th minute. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall provided the cross and Barry lashed home from close range for his seventh goal this season. item.description: Chieftains of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) have urged Nigerians to mobilise grassroots support for the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, come 2027. The party chieftains, including a political economist, Prof Pat Utomi, Enugu State NDC governorship candidate, Chief Chinyeaka Ohaa and human rights activist, Aisha Yesufu, made the call on Thursday during the Obi-Kwankwaso Town Hall Meeting held in Enugu. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Obi, his running mate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, and other NDC stakeholders attended the meeting, which attracted a large crowd of supporters. Addressing the crowd, Utomi expressed confidence that the Obi-Kwankwaso presidential ticket would provide the leadership needed to address Nigeria’s economic, political and security challenges. He lamented that Nigeria’s potential to become one of the greatest countries in the world had been undermined by corruption, criminality and disunity. According to him, the time has come for Nigerians to unite and work towards achieving meaningful political change. “We have done our research, and I know that a combination of Peter Gregory Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso will deliver Nigeria,” he said. Utomi urged Nigerians to turn out massively during the elections, vote for their preferred candidates and defend their votes through lawful means. In his remarks, Ohaa, the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, described the Obi-Kwankwaso political alliance as a historic opportunity to strengthen national unity and promote inclusive governance. He said the partnership represented the possibility of building political bridges across Nigeria’s geopolitical zones. According to him, the alliance is reminiscent of the historic political understanding between the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe and Sir Ahmadu Bello during Nigeria’s early political development. “My message today is simple: we must seize this opportunity and work with our brothers and sisters across the South-South, South-West, North-East, North-West and North-Central to secure an NDC president in 2027,” he said. Ohaa explained that the campaign was not merely about producing a president of Igbo extraction but about establishing a government committed to justice, accountability, security and prosperity for all Nigerians. He expressed confidence that NDC candidates in Enugu State were prepared to earn the trust of voters and secure victory in the elections. Yesufu, a human rights activist, urged Nigerians to take ownership of the 2027 elections by mobilising voters and actively participating in the democratic process. She said the election was not merely about Obi’s presidential ambition but about the collective responsibility of Nigerians to rescue the country from its numerous challenges. item.title: I’ll work closely with Kwankwaso if elected, Obi reassures
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has reiterated willingness to work closely with his vice-presidential candidate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, to move the country forward. Obi gave the assurance on Thursday during a town hall meeting in Enugu, where he engaged supporters and stakeholders on the country’s challenges and his vision for national development. The former Anambra State governor said they would work together to tackle insecurity and restore safety across Nigeria if elected president in 2027. He said that securing lives and property would be a priority of his administration, promising to confront the security challenges threatening communities and livelihoods across the country. The presidential candidate regretted that the current administration had failed to protect the lives and property of Nigerians, which he maintained was the primary responsibility. Obi assured voters in the South East to vote for him because of his competence and ability to tackle challenges facing the nation. He challenged other presidential candidates to meet and discuss their plans, and warned the people not to be deceived by rhetoric and propaganda. On education, Obi said he would declare a state of emergency on education to enable his administration to tackle the issue of out-of-school children head-on, hinting that Nigerian children deserved quality education. In his remarks, the vice-presidential candidate of NDC, Kwankwaso, advised that nobody should be deceived by ethnicity, saying, “It’s obvious that Nigerians are going through numerous difficulties”. Kwankwaso lamented that people were facing challenges like insecurity, unemployment, poverty, hunger and so many other challenges. He explained that the only solution to achieve a new Nigeria was unity, diligence, perseverance and willingness. He urged Nigerians to come out en masse to cast, protect and follow up on their votes until results were announced, noting that it was not a one-man show but a collective responsibility. Also, Sen Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly, described Obi and his running mate, Kwankwaso, as the “best presidential ticket” to lead Nigeria. Umeh expressed confidence that the South-East would rally behind Obi in the 2027 presidential election, urging the people to remain resolute and resist attempts to intimidate or discourage them from pursuing their political choice. He also commended the resilience of supporters who, according to him, ensured that the meeting held despite reported attempts to frustrate the gathering. The senator further praised Kwankwaso for his efforts to build support in Northern Nigeria, expressing optimism that the Obi-led ticket could attract votes across the country. Umeh urged the people of the South-East to use their votes to make a strong political statement in 2027, declaring his support for Obi’s presidential ambition and calling on the region to unite behind the project. item.title: FROM DRY TAPS TO RUNNING WATER: GOVERNOR ABBA KABIR YUSUF’S WATER LEGACY
item.description: By Farida Usman For generations, reliable public water supply has remained one of Kano’s most persistent development challenges. Across the ancient city, surrounding communities and expanding residential layouts, households have endured irregular supply, long searches for water and the uncertainty of when their taps would run again. For many residents, access to water became a daily struggle rather than a basic public service. That reality is beginning to change under Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, as the state’s water infrastructure rehabilitation moves from construction to service delivery; With the Challawa and Tamburawa treatment plants and their pumping stations reported to be 100 per cent complete, a successful test run conducted and water flow commenced, Kano has reached a significant milestone in its effort to restore dependable public water supply and its system. The achievement is important, but its real value lies in what it means for ordinary Bakano. Water must not merely be treated and pumped; it must reach homes, schools, hospitals, markets and businesses consistently. The administration’s next task is therefore to translate restored infrastructure into reliable and consistent supply across the communities that depend on it. Significantly, the test run has exposed reticulation challenges in parts of the distribution network across many locations in the state due to non-use of the pipes. These are now being addressed. Rather than diminishing the achievement, identifying these gaps provides a practical basis for targeted repairs and improvements. The ultimate measure of success will be how effectively the government closes these gaps and extends the benefits of the restored facilities to underserved neighbourhoods and communities. For communities such as Dukawa, Kofar Wambai and Shehi, as well as semi-urban settlements and newer layouts around Tamburawa, the expectation is clear: water should flow reliably, safely and affordably. Completing treatment plants is a major step; ensuring that the distribution network delivers their output to the intended users is the test that follows. The benefits of dependable water supply reach far beyond household convenience. Children can spend less time fetching water and more time learning. Families can reduce their reliance on costly alternatives, health facilities can improve hygiene, and small businesses can operate with fewer interruptions. Investment in water is therefore an investment in public health, education, productivity and human dignity and prosperity. sacrosanct, the restoration of infrastructure must not be mistaken for the complete resolution of Kano’s water challenges. The state’s growing population, expanding urban settlements and the continuing cost of operating and maintaining major facilities demand sustained attention. item.title: Inter, AC Milan unveil new stadium plans to replace San Siro
item.description: Inter and AC Milan unveiled their new “Generali Stadium” Thursday, which will replace the iconic San Siro stadium from the 2031/32 season. It will be shaped “low in the body, and it rises up at either end” behind the goals, architect Norman Foster said during a press conference in Milan. The design aims to bring spectators as close to the pitch as possible, with the stands behind the goals set at a steep 37-degree incline, said David Manica, a stadium specialist who collaborated with Foster on the project. “The most important thing that we realised when we designed this project is that the San Siro is a feeling,” he said. “It’s more than a building, it’s a feeling, and everything that we needed to do here was to carry it into the (new) building”. Manica said the design team “started with proximity”. “We brought all the seats as close as possible to the field. They could not be any closer, it’ll actually feel as though you’re sitting on the grass,” he said. They also paid great attention to acoustics: the roof covers the stands, leaving only the pitch exposed, and is designed to “amplify the roar” of the fans, Manica said. “This building is steeper than many other new buildings are built today, and that’s intentional, because it allows us to bring those seats up and over the field as much as possible, and create that sense of intimacy and atmosphere,” he said. The stadium, sponsored by the Italian insurance giant Generali, will also be capable of hosting American football games, rugby matches and concerts. “I want the crowd to come to the new stadium and to feel that excitement that they felt before, and to feel the building, living and breathing with them as it does currently,” Manica said. AC Milan and Inter paid 197 million euros ($219 million) to acquire the current stadium and its adjacent parking areas, where they intend to build their new, shared home. The project for the new San Siro — which will have a capacity of 71,500 seats, compared to the current 75,000 — will cost the two clubs 1.2 billion euros. Construction is set to begin in 2028. Foster and Manica previously worked together on London’s Wembley Stadium. Milan’s current stadium — one of the most iconic in European football and often likened to a “concrete cathedral” — is the largest in Italy. But the venue, which opened in 1926, no longer meets the needs of spectators or the clubs, despite undergoing several renovations over the decades. San Siro, also known as the Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, will be largely demolished once construction work on the new stadium nears completion. item.title: 2027: INEC grants provisional clearance to Pantami, Gwarzo – Source
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi & Ben Ngwakwe There were strong indications on Thursday night that the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC might have provisionally cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Gombe State, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections. The clearance of both men is subject to the outcome of pending court cases, it was learned on Thursday night. In Gombe, Pantami’s supporters took over some major areas celebrating the development on Thursday night. INEC officials did not immediately react to Vanguard’s questions regarding the development. But a source said the decisions were reached at the commission’s meeting on Thursday to consider complaints from political parties and candidates whose names were left out of the lists published ahead of the 2027 elections. The source added that the commission had no objection to their candidacies, but that the pending legal proceedings could still affect the final outcome. The development comes after INEC dropped Pantami’s name from the final list of governorship candidates for Gombe State, although he appeared on the provisional list published on August 29. Pantami emerged as the PDP candidate after leaving the All Progressives Congress (APC) on May 19. One of the aspirants for the ticket, Ahmed Mailantarki Mailantarki, challenged his victory in court. A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which Pantami won again. His biggest hurdle was the September 24 Supreme Court judgement, which restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. The provisions bar parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time. Mohammed Haruna, an INEC National Commissioner, had previously said that, in line with the Supreme Court ruling, some parties would not field candidates in 2027. The commission, however, rejected a petition by the PDP governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, who had asked it to review his exclusion from the list of candidates. item.title: ‘Star Trek’, ‘X-Men’ star Patrick Stewart dies at 86
item.description: Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died at the age of 86, an official statement said Thursday. “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement said. The actor, who hailed from the northern English region of Yorkshire, trod the boards in Britain with the Royal Shakespeare Company before crossing the Atlantic to enjoy an acclaimed career on the US stage and screen. His best known Hollywood roles were as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and Professor Charles Xavier in multiple “X-Men” and related Marvel films. “His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the statement said. “He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.” AFP The post ‘Star Trek’, ‘X-Men’ star Patrick Stewart dies at 86 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: [VIDEO] Umrah: Tinubu Arrives In Saudi Arabia
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has arrived in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The President landed at the King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, on Thursday night. ﻿ He was received by the Nigerian ambassador to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and Saudi’s head of Royal Protocol, Ahmad bin Thafir. Tinubu is in the country to perform Umrah, an Islamic spiritual exercise involving a pilgrimage to the Holy City. He departed Abuja for Makkah on Thursday afternoon. The event is an opportunity for spiritual reflection, devotion, and prayers for the nation’s peace, unity, stability, and continued progress, Tinubu’s media aide, Bayo Onanuga, said in a statement on Wednesday. According to the statement, the President will perform the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. He is expected back in the country next week. The post [VIDEO] Umrah: Tinubu Arrives In Saudi Arabia appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Troops neutralise two high-profile ISWAP leaders, others in Borno
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The troops of Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have killed 15 Boko Haram terrorists, including two (2) prominent ISWAP Qayids, Abu Musanna and Hassan Abu Huraira in Kerenoa, Marte Local Government Area of Borno State. This is as the Theatre Commander of OPHK, Major General Ibikunle Ajose on Thursday commissioned the newly constructed three blocks of 12-family Corporals and Below Quarters (CBQ) at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri. The commissioning forms part of activities to commemorate the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu’s one year in office, which also reflects his commitment to improving troops’ living conditions, strengthening morale and enhancing operational effectiveness. In a press statement signed by the Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni on Thursday said: “Troops of OPHK continued to record operational successes through sustained intelligence-led offensive operations aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities and dismantling their networks across the theatre. “In a further operation, OPHK air assets, at about 9:20 pm on 28 October 2026, conducted an armed reconnaissance and air interdiction mission in the Kerenoa Marte Local Government Area of Borno State, resulting in the neutralisation of 15 terrorists and the destruction of an IED hideout. “The mission followed intelligence reports on terrorist activities in the area. During the operation, the air assets tracked two terrorists on a motorcycle to a makeshift structure beneath a tree. Further surveillance revealed additional movements around the location, indicating the presence of other terrorists. Consequently, the location was engaged with precision strikes. “Following the strikes, Battle Damage Assessment (BDA) indicated that 15 terrorists were neutralised, while structures at the location were destroyed. Additionally, a secondary fire observed after the engagement suggested that the targeted structure may have been used for the storage of terrorist IED logistics hub. “It has been confirmed that 2 prominent ISWAP Qayids, Abu Musanna and Hassan Abu Huraira were amongst those neutralised while several other fighters were severely wounded, including the Wali (ISWAP Governor) of the area who is reported to be critically injured. “The operation forms part of OPHK’s sustained intelligence-led air offensive aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities, disrupting their hideouts and dismantling logistics networks across the theatre. The Joint Task Force continues to conduct coordinated operations against terrorist elements in the North East to achieve its Operational mandate of restoring total and long-lasting peace in the region,” Goni stated. item.title: Just In: Tinubu lands in Saudi Arabia for Umrah
item.description: President Bola Tinubu on Thursday evening arrived in Saudi Arabia, landing at the King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah. He was received by Nigeria’s ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and the Saudi head of royal protocol Ahmad bin Thafir. The President is scheduled to perform Umrah, also known as the lesser hajj, and is expected to return to Nigeria next week after completing the religious exercise. Thursday’s trip marks the second time Tinubu has travelled to Makkah to perform Umrah since assuming office on May 29, 2023. President Tinubu visited the holy city in November 2023, shortly after attending the Saudi-African Summit in Riyadh, where he also prayed for divine guidance in leading Nigeria. The latest trip is part of a series of foreign engagements undertaken by Tinubu since becoming president. He has visited more than 30 countries in over 50 unique and recurring trips. item.title: 2027: Tinubu Can Be Sure Of Victory In Imo With My Name On Ballot — Okorocha
item.description: Former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win Imo State in the 2027 presidential election if he is on the ballot as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Imo West Senatorial District. Okorocha is locked in a legal battle with his successor, Governor Hope Uzodimma, over the APC ticket for Imo West, with both laying claim to victory in the party’s primary election. ﻿ The APC, however, submitted Uzodimma’s name to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as its candidate, prompting Okorocha to challenge the decision in court. On Thursday, the Federal Capital Territory High Court ruled that Okorocha secured the majority of votes cast in the primary and should be declared the winner. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today hours after the judgment, Okorocha said his presence on the ballot would guarantee Tinubu’s victory in the state. “What is important to me now is how Asiwaju will be elected in Imo State. With this, my name coming on the ballot paper now, Asiwaju can be sure that his victory is given in Imo State,” he said. The former governor celebrated the ruling, insisting that the judiciary was not for sale. He also said Uzodimma had “met his Waterloo,” alleging that the court had pronounced that his documents “were forged”. Okorocha urged people in the South-East to approach the 2027 presidential election strategically, advising the Igbo to put political calculations ahead of emotions. According to him, supporting Tinubu would amount to a strategic alliance that could benefit the South-East politically in the future. “As Southeasterners, we are not going to politics now with emotions; we have to go to politics with strategy. So, supporting Tinubu for Ndigbo is a strategic alliance,” he said. “We cannot afford to gamble for four years. Any time Nigerians think it is the time for Ndigbo to be president, we should be proper presidents.” Okorocha added that he would work more effectively with other South-East governors to secure Tinubu’s victory in the region if he were placed in charge of the president’s campaign in Imo State. item.title: Germany’s Zverev becomes tennis world No. 1
item.description: Alexander Zverev accelerated his ascension to number one in the world rankings for the first time in his career on Thursday as he beat Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 to reach the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open. The 29-year-old German was already assured of finishing the season top of the ATP rankings but, in the absence of current incumbent Jannik Sinner, two-time Grand Slam champion Zverev will now take that crown in next week’s updated standings after winning his opening two matches in the Austrian capital. Long seen as tennis’ nearly-man, Zverev has enjoyed a stellar 2026, breaking his major duck by picking up the titles at the French and US Opens. Now he has broken further ground by becoming only the 30th man to claim top spot since the rankings were first published in 1973. He will be aged 29 years and 196 days when Monday’s new rankings are published, making him the second-oldest first-time number one after Australian John Newcombe. Due to a knee injury Italy’s Sinner decided to end his season at the start of October, opening the way for Zverev to dethrone him. And the big-serving Hamburg native ensured he did just that ahead of the season-ending ATP Finals next month by seeing off Martin Landaluce and Griekspoor in his opening two matches in Vienna. Zverev needed to save four match points against Spain’s Landaluce in his first-round match on Tuesday, but was much more comfortable as he defeated Griekspoor in straight sets to write his name into the history books. He raced out of the blocks on Thursday, breaking the 30-year-old Dutchman in the very first game and then confidently serving his way into a one-set lead. The second frame went to 5-5 before Zverev pounced on Griekspoor’s serve to get his nose in front. The match met an unexpected stoppage as Zverev brought up match point when a smash off the German’s racquet caused part of the electronic board behind Griekspoor to malfunction. But once the umpire covered the problematic panel up with a towel, Zverev then sealed his new ranking with an unreturnable serve. item.title: Awujale succession: DSS invites Fusengbuwa ruling house leaders
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Department of State Services (DSS) in Ogun State has reportedly invited three leaders of the Fusengbuwa ruling house over the alleged sale of expression-of-interest forms to princes seeking to become the next Awujale of Ijebuland. Those reportedly invited are the Chairman of the ruling house, Otunba Abdulateef Owoyemi; the deputy chairman, Otunba Dokun Ajidagba; and the vice chairman, Prof. Fassy Yusuf. The invitation comes amid an ongoing dispute over the selection of a new Awujale following the death of the previous monarch, Oba Sikiru Adetona, in July 2025, at the age of 91, after 65 years on the throne. A letter circulating online, purportedly signed by one Yemi Oloto, directed the three ruling house leaders to appear before the State Director of Security at the DSS office in Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta, on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 4 p.m. The letter, which indicated that the meeting was connected with an investigation into the sale of expression-of-interest forms to princes interested in the vacant stool, read in part: “I am directed to invite you for a meeting with the State Director of Security (SDS), Department of State Services (DSS), Ogun State, Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta, today, 29th October, 2026, 1600 hours (4 p.m.). “The meeting is in furtherance of investigating activities in respect of the sale of expression-of-interest forms to interested princes for the vacant stool of Awujale of Ijebuland.” The letter further stated that an officer had been designated at the main gate to facilitate the invitees’ entry into the premises, before concluding with the director’s best wishes. When contacted, Prof. Yusuf confirmed receiving the invitation but said he was in Abuja attending to a matter before the Supreme Court and would therefore be unable to honour it. The professor of Mass Communication and lawyer said: “I just received the letter from the DSS not long ago, but I am in Abuja attending to a matter at the Supreme Court. I have discountenanced their letter.” Similarly, Ajidagba confirmed receiving the invitation on Thursday afternoon, saying it was delivered at about 2:30 p.m. with instructions to report at the DSS office by 4:30 p.m. He, however, questioned the timing of the invitation, arguing that matters relating to the succession process were already before the courts. “I received the DSS invitation on Thursday at about 2:30 p.m., and I was told to report at their office by 4:30 p.m. There was, however, no way I could honour such an invitation when all of these matters are already in court. The status quo must be allowed to remain; that is the position of the law,” he said. There was no immediate confirmation from the DSS on the reported invitations or the allegations prompting them. The latest development comes against the backdrop of previous engagements between security agencies and stakeholders in the Awujale succession process. item.title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Stablecoins here to optimise financial system, not replace it’
item.description: By Efosa Taiwo Stablecoins could transform cross-border payments by reducing transaction delays, improving liquidity and making money transfers faster and more accessible, speakers at Moonshot 2026 have said. The speakers made the remarks during a panel session titled “The New Payment Backbone: Stablecoins as Core Infrastructure for Global Liquidity” on the Emerging Tech Stage, where industry leaders discussed how stablecoins could reshape payments across Africa and the global financial system. Mercy Emmanuel, Stablecoin & Blockchain Vertical Lead, Flutterwave, said stablecoins could simplify international transfers, which often involve multiple intermediaries and take several days to complete. “Sending money from Lagos to Nairobi goes through a lot. It could take two to five days before it gets to its destination. Stablecoins collapse all these,” Emmanuel said. She likened the technology to a moving train that operates without the restrictions of banking hours and time zones, arguing that it could make payments almost instantaneous and allow businesses to conduct transactions seamlessly alongside their online operations. According to her, stablecoins could also encourage businesses to rethink their payment processes and build more efficient financial operations. “Stablecoins are here to optimise the financial system, not displace the traditional way,” she said, adding that the financial industry was moving towards a system in which the focus would be on how quickly and efficiently money could move from one point to another. Tayo Oviosu, Group Chief Executive Officer of Paga, said widespread stablecoin adoption would require collaboration among financial technology companies, sufficient liquidity and simpler access for everyday users. He argued that consumers were more concerned about the cost and speed of financial services than the underlying technology powering their transactions. “Ultimately, it is giving them what they want: they want to go from fiat to fiat. Stablecoin can be used in between,” he said. Oviosu added that solving liquidity challenges would make stablecoin transactions easier to access and use, stressing that no single company could independently make the technology a mainstream part of everyday financial life. “We want to make it simple. The way you can come to Paga and get a naira wallet, get a stablecoin wallet. That is the part of the user,” he said. He also called for industry players to work together to expand the use of stablecoins, noting that stronger collaboration would be necessary to improve access to the infrastructure and liquidity required to support wider adoption. Ife Johnson, co-founder of JuicyWay, also emphasised the need for shared infrastructure, urging industry players to move away from isolated systems towards solutions that could support the wider financial ecosystem. “The mind shift that needs to happen is moving from silos to shared infrastructure for industry players,” Johnson said. item.title: Grealish dropped for Everton’s League Cup tie after disciplinary breach
item.description: Jack Grealish was dropped for Everton’s League Cup fourth round clash against Newcastle on Thursday after “a breach of club discipline”. It was reported that the breach related to Grealish’s unauthorised absence from training. The 31-year-old missed Saturday’s 2-0 loss at Arsenal in the Premier League due to an illness. Grealish, who is on a second season-long loan from Manchester City, had started Everton’s three Premier League matches prior to their defeat against champions Arsenal. The 31-year-old has made six appearances for David Moyes’s side this term, most recently in their loss against Chelsea on October 17. Grealish has been dogged by criticism of his off-pitch behaviour for several years amid reports of nightclub incidents that saw him fall out of favour at City. After playing a key role in City’s treble-winning campaign in 2022-23, Grealish became an increasingly sidelined figure at the Etihad Stadium. Everton are facing Newcastle for a place in the League Cup quarter-finals, with Fleetwood awaiting the winner after their shock victory over Arsenal on Tuesday. item.title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Africa must move from content creation to value capture’ — Tech leader Juliet Ehimuan
item.description: By Efosa Taiwo Juliet Ehimuan, founder of Beyond Limits and former Director of Google West Africa, has urged African creatives and technology entrepreneurs to move beyond content creation to building sustainable businesses that own intellectual property and capture value from their work. Ehimuan made the call while speaking on artificial intelligence (AI) and the future of African creativity at Moonshot 2026 during a keynote speech on Thursday. She said Africa’s creative economy remained underdeveloped, stressing the need to turn the continent’s creative talent into commercially viable enterprises capable of generating greater economic value. “Our creative economy is still less than 2% of GDP,” she said, highlighting the need for a shift from producing content to building businesses around it. According to her, African creators must focus on owning the intellectual property behind their work and exploring different ways to commercialise it. “We need to move from content creation to value capture. We need to move from having creative talents to building enterprises. We should move from content creation to IP,” Ehimuan said. She explained that intellectual property ownership could open up multiple revenue streams, noting that a book could be adapted into a series, while a podcast could generate additional commercial opportunities. “There are so many ways to monetise content if you have the IP for that,” she said, emphasising the importance of owning intellectual property and the infrastructure needed to distribute and commercialise creative products. Ehimuan outlined three priorities for Africa’s creative and technology sectors: adopting and developing AI capabilities, building and owning valuable assets, and establishing businesses capable of reaching wider markets. On AI adoption, she encouraged African businesses to develop their capabilities and stay ahead of technological changes, noting that the technology could improve productivity and create new opportunities across industries. She also urged creators and businesses to protect their rights and permissions while developing distinctive intellectual property that could be commercialised over time. item.title: ‘One in 4 Nigerian stroke patients under 50’
item.description: One in four stroke cases in Nigeria affects people below 50, raising concerns about the disease’s growing burden among young adults. Prof. Kolawole Wahab, Head of the Stroke Unit at the University of Ilorin Teaching Hospital (UITH), disclosed this on Thursday in Ilorin. He spoke on the sidelines of a medical rally commemorating the 2026 World Stroke Day, with the theme ‘Every Minute Counts’, which highlights the importance of prompt treatment. Wahab said research published in 2017 had documented the prevalence of stroke among younger Nigerians. “When we talk about stroke in the young, we are talking about those who are below the age of 50. “One out of every four cases of stroke in Nigeria could be a case of stroke in the young. The prevalence is as high as 25 per cent. “We see people who are in their 40s, some in their 30s, coming down with stroke,” he said. The neurologist described the stroke burden in the region as epidemic, adding that UITH’s emergency department receives one or two stroke patients daily. He identified hypertension as Nigeria’s leading stroke risk factor, warning that poor blood pressure control could increase the likelihood of the condition. According to him, up to nine out of every 10 stroke cases have hypertension as an underlying factor. Wahab expressed concern that some patients abandon prescribed medication in favour of unproven remedies, leaving their blood pressure uncontrolled. He also identified diabetes as another major risk factor, noting that some people remain unaware they have the condition. Others, he said, neglect proper diabetes management in spite of knowing their status. “It is until they have suffered from stroke that they become aware they have diabetes,” he said. Wahab listed imbalances in blood fats among other risk factors, explaining that abnormal levels of good and bad fats could contribute to stroke. He warned against smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, hard drugs and sedentary lifestyles, urging Nigerians to adopt healthier habits. The expert also advised people to moderate their salt intake, particularly those diagnosed with hypertension. He cautioned against adding table salt to meals after preparation, stressing the importance of controlling blood pressure. Also speaking, Dr Wemimo Olaofin, a consultant neurologist at UITH, urged Nigerians to check their blood pressure regularly. Olaofin said stroke could occur suddenly at any time, but preventive measures and proper health management could reduce the risk. He encouraged the public to monitor their blood pressure and embrace healthier lifestyles to prevent the condition. Mrs Tejumola Olayinka, Deputy Director of Nursing in charge of UITH’s Stroke Care Unit, said the commemoration aimed to promote awareness and early hospital presentation. “Stroke case is an emergency case that requires timely intervention. item.title: Falana seeks recovery of $123bn in oil funds
item.description: Human rights lawyer, Femi Falana, SAN, has called for the recovery of more than $123 billion and N66.4 billion allegedly owed to the Federation Account by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and other oil and gas companies. Falana, in a letter dated October 28, 2026, addressed to the Senate President and copied to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, urged the authorities to initiate measures to recover the funds, which he said comprised outstanding oil royalties, proceeds of alleged crude oil theft, unpaid dividends, taxes and other revenues. The senior lawyer warned that failure to initiate recovery measures within 14 days of receiving the letter would prompt his firm to institute legal proceedings at the Federal High Court to compel the relevant authorities to act. The letter, signed by Falana, outlined five categories of alleged outstanding funds and cited court judgments, government reports and legislative investigations in support of the demand. On royalties, Falana said an estimated $62 billion had remained uncollected from international oil companies over 18 years following the non-implementation of provisions of the Deep Offshore and Inland Basin Production Sharing Contracts Act. He cited a Supreme Court consent judgment delivered on October 20, 2018, directing the Federal Government to collect outstanding royalties under the law and pay oil-producing states their 13 per cent derivation entitlements upon recovery. According to the letter, the Federal High Court subsequently entered judgments in favour of Akwa Ibom and Rivers states for a combined $3.3 billion, while Bayelsa State obtained a separate judgment for $951 million. Falana alleged that the Federal Government had yet to comply with the judgments. On alleged crude oil theft and undeclared exports, he cited findings attributed to a team of Nigerian lawyers engaged by the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency, which reportedly identified about 60.2 million barrels of crude oil, valued at $12.7 billion, allegedly discharged at a port in Philadelphia, United States, between 2011 and 2014. He also referred to a House of Representatives ad hoc committee’s investigation into undeclared crude oil and liquefied natural gas exports during the same period. According to the letter, the committee found that oil and gas exports worth $17 billion had been shipped without proper records. Falana urged the authorities to pursue the recovery of the combined $29 billion from the companies allegedly involved, while acknowledging that civil cases filed by NIMASA were pending before the Federal High Court. The lawyer further alleged that NNPCL had failed to remit $23.1 billion in dividends attributable to the Federal Government’s 49 per cent stake in Nigeria LNG Limited to the Federation Account. item.title: Anyaoku condemns xenophobic attacks in South Africa
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief Former Commonwealth Secretary-General, Chief Emeka Anyaoku, has condemned the reported xenophobic attacks against African nationals in South Africa, describing them as distressing and regrettable. Anyaoku expressed sadness that South Africans, who endured years of apartheid and received support from across Africa in their struggle for liberation, were now turning against fellow Africans from other countries. The 94-year-old statesman spoke in an interview on the sidelines of the MasterClass on Penetrative Leadership in an Increasingly Chaotic World Order in Abuja. He recalled his role in efforts to end apartheid and facilitate negotiations between the former white-minority government and the country’s black majority, saying the current attacks were particularly painful given the sacrifices made by other African countries. “The attacks are regrettable,” Anyaoku said, recalling how he worked to secure support from Commonwealth leaders for efforts to facilitate negotiations in South Africa following the release of Nelson Mandela in 1990. He recounted that Mandela visited Abuja in May 1990 for a meeting of Commonwealth foreign ministers responsible for South Africa and attended his first official dinner as secretary-general. Anyaoku said the visit marked the beginning of a friendship with Mandela and his then-wife, Winnie Mandela. He explained that in 1991, he secured a mandate from Commonwealth Heads of Government to visit South Africa and explore ways to help the country’s then-president, F.W. de Klerk, organise talks aimed at ending apartheid. According to him, his meeting with de Klerk on November 1, 1991, focused on rebuilding confidence among South Africa’s major ethnic groups. Anyaoku said de Klerk initially questioned how the Commonwealth could assist South Africa, given its support for sanctions against the apartheid government. He said he explained that the Commonwealth could help build confidence among the country’s black, white and Asian communities, using the diversity of his delegation as an example. Anyaoku added that he intervened when the negotiations threatened to collapse, helping to keep the process on course. He recalled that the agreement concluding the negotiations was signed at 3:30 a.m. on November 17, 1993, in his presence. item.title: 2027: Obi pledges 10,000 MW of power, declares emergency on corruption
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu Presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, has pledged to generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected president in 2027, promising to tackle insecurity, corruption, unemployment and other challenges confronting the country. Obi, who made the pledge during a Town hall meeting in Enugu, also promised to declare emergencies in education and the fight against corruption, while ensuring access to primary healthcare in every ward across the country. He said Nigeria needed a leader with the competence, capacity, compassion, commitment and character to address its economic and security challenges and restore public confidence in governance. According to him, the country is currently battling widespread hunger, unemployment and insecurity, making the 2027 presidential election critical to its future. “Today, our country is suffering. Today, people are hungry. Today, our children do not have employment. Today, Nigeria is not secure,” Obi said. He urged Nigerians to elect a president capable of uniting the country, securing lives and property, and creating an environment for economic growth and development. The former Anambra State governor said his administration would take decisive action against insecurity, insisting that the government must confront criminal elements wherever they operate. “As president of Nigeria, I will unite Nigeria. As president of Nigeria, I will secure Nigeria. We will deal with security,” he declared. On corruption, Obi said public funds must be deployed for the benefit of citizens, promising greater transparency and accountability in government expenditure and borrowing. “People must stop stealing public money. Public money must be used for public good. That is why I am making my commitment. We will be accountable, we will be open,” he said. He added that Nigerians would be informed about the purpose of government borrowing and how borrowed funds were spent. On education and healthcare, the NDC presidential candidate promised to ensure that children had access to schooling and that every ward in the country had primary healthcare services. Obi also identified electricity as a major priority of his proposed administration, arguing that reliable power supply was necessary to revive industries, create jobs and stimulate economic activities. “As I promised, we will generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity, because we want industrial work,” he said, urging Nigerians not to lose hope in the country’s future. item.title: Paris Gun Attack Leaves One Dead, Five Wounded As Suspect Faces Terrorism Probe
item.description: A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week that killed one person and wounded five including a child has admitted to “targeting individuals who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African,” prosecutors said on Thursday. Earlier this week the 39-year-old man, identified as Kevin T., had said he did not “dispute the material facts”, but contested “the racist nature of his crimes”. On Thursday, national terrorism prosecutor Olivier Christen told a news conference that Kevin T. now claims he chose the location for his actions because it was “a hotbed for Islamists”. The victims were shot from a vehicle driving through the towns of Trappes and La Verriere west of Paris. The suspect was detained later Friday with a machine gun and tear-gas grenades in his car. He has since been held in police custody and was set to appear before a judge later on Thursday, Christen said, noting that he had requested that he be held in pretrial detention. France’s counter-terrorism public prosecutor Olivier Christen speaks during a press conference at the Paris Judicial Court, in Paris on October 29, 2026, following the terrorist attack that took place on October 23 in Trappes and La Verriere.Photo by ANNE-CHRISTINE POUJOULAT / AFP Of the four people seriously injured in the attack, “three of the victims remain hospitalised as I speak, and one of them is still in life-threatening condition,” Christen said. He noted the “very high level of preparation” behind the attack. Kevin T. nevertheless denied any “terrorist intent,” viewing his actions as “legitimate,” the prosecutor said. The opening of a judicial investigation by the office of the national anti-terrorism prosecutor (PNAT) allows a judge to take charge of the case, specifically regarding charges of “murder and attempted murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise”. A search of the suspect’s home had uncovered “weapons or weapon components, specifically a magazine, two pairs of brass knuckles, a steel bayonet, and a silencer,” Christen said. Also found were several “books, including a Quran, a Bible, and Adolf Hitler’s Mein Kampf”, as well as stickers celebrating the far-right National Rally (RN) party. Christen said the stickers bore slogans such as “Long live France, RN, proud to be French”, but they were not produced by the party led by Marine Le Pen, who is leading opinion polls to succeed Emmanuel Macron as French president in elections next spring. Kevin T. had told investigators that “he designed the stickers found in his home himself, and then ordered them to be manufactured via Amazon more than a year ago.” The suspect had said that “he is neither a member of nor a sympathiser with any political party”, Christen said.
